extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning homological algebra and algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and exercises developing Tor, Ext, derived functors, δ-functors, spectral sequences, and derived functor cohomology of O-modules; aimed at constructing and computing these invariants and understanding their formal properties and constructions (horseshoe, Cartan–Eilenberg, Grothendieck spectral sequence, Leray).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of Tor from choice of resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor^A_i(M,N) (constructed using a projective/free resolution R of N) does not depend on the choice of resolution: given two resolutions R and R' there are lifts f_R: R -> R' and f_R': R' -> R whose compositions are homotopic to the identity, inducing canonical isomorphisms Tor^A_i(M,N)_R -> Tor^A_i(M,N)_R'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: choose lifts of the identity map on N and use homotopies to show the maps induced on homology are canonical isomorphisms; this shows Tor is well-defined independent of the resolution choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tor is a covariant functor
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed M, Tor^A_i(M, ·) is a covariant additive functor Mod_A -> Mod_A (and similarly in the other variable once symmetry is established).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks/notes: functoriality comes from functoriality of resolutions and the induced maps; additivity and long exact sequences follow from construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing of Tor with free modules
rubrics_metrics.description: If N is a free module, then Tor^A_i(M,N) = 0 for all i > 0 (N is its own trivial resolution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as basic building block: free/projective modules give vanishing of higher Tor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence for Tor from short exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any short exact sequence of A-modules 0 -> N' -> N -> N'' -> 0 we obtain a long exact sequence of Tor's (Proposition 23.1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: take resolutions of N' and N'' and use the horseshoe construction to get a short exact sequence of resolutions for N, truncate, tensor with M, and take homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horseshoe construction for resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given short exact sequence 0 -> N' -> N -> N'' -> 0 with projective/free resolutions for N' and N'', one can construct a projective/free resolution for N by 'filling in' a middle row (the horseshoe), yielding a short exact sequence of resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: middle row maps are block upper triangular; one may need to choose lifts of certain maps (exercise 23.1.B). Used to derive long exact sequences in Tor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness equivalent conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A-module M the following are equivalent: (i) M is flat; (ii) Tor^A_1(M,N) = 0 for all A-modules N; (iii) Tor^A_i(M,N) = 0 for all i > 0 and all A-modules N (Exercise 23.1.C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution: one might be tempted to deduce some implications using symmetry of Tor; symmetry for i>0 is proved later (Exercise 23.3.A), so be careful in arguments that rely on Tor(N,M) = Tor(M,N).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of connecting homomorphism δ
rubrics_metrics.description: The connecting homomorphism δ in the long exact sequences (obtained from horseshoe, truncation, tensor, homology) is independent of choices of resolutions and lifts (Exercise 23.1.D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested approach: compare two constructions by building a map (a 3-dimensional diagram) between the two versions to show equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective object / module lifting property
rubrics_metrics.description: A module P is projective iff for every surjection M -> N any morphism P -> N lifts to P -> M (diagram (23.2.1.1)). Equivalently Hom(P, ·) is exact (or left-exact and preserves surjections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises: show projective iff direct summand of a free module (23.2.A) and projective modules are flat (hint: use 23.2.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of derived functors via projective resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a right-exact covariant functor, then its left derived functors LiF (i ≥ 0) are defined by applying F to projective resolutions: L0F = F and the LiF's fit into long exact sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes the abelian category has enough projectives (surjections from projectives onto any object). The construction uses lifting repeatedly and preservation of products by F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and duality for derived functors
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is right-exact, its left derived functors are LiF (subscript); if F is left-exact, its right derived functors are RiF (superscript). The index direction indicates ascending i in long exact sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep careful track of whether deriving left or right and the corresponding notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition(s) of Ext functors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ext^i_A(M,N) may be defined in two equivalent ways: (D) as the ith right derived functor of Hom(·,N) applied to M (contravariant left-exact in first variable); (E) as the ith right derived functor of Hom(M,·) applied to N (covariant left-exact in second variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 23.3.B shows the two definitions agree; each definition gives a corresponding long exact sequence in Ext.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness of Ext over Noetherian rings
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian and M,N are finitely generated A-modules, then Ext^i_A(M,N) is a finitely generated A-module (Exercise 23.2.F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses definition via derived functors and properties of Noetherian rings and finitely generated modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enough injectives in Mod_A and Mod_OX
rubrics_metrics.description: The category Mod_A of A-modules has enough injectives; similarly, for a ringed space (X,O_X), Mod_OX has enough injectives (Theorem 23.4.1 and Section 23.2.5 discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction/Proof hints: injective Z-modules are divisible; use Hom_Z(A,Q) to produce injective A-modules; for sheaves use skyscraper sheaves at stalks and products of injectives (Exercises 23.2.I–K and 23.4.A–C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Injective object definition (dual to projective)
rubrics_metrics.description: An object Q is injective iff for every inclusion (monomorphism) M ↪ N any morphism M -> Q extends to N -> Q. This notion is dual to projective; see Exercise 23.2.C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful facts: quotients of injective Z-modules are injective (23.2.H), and right adjoints to exact functors preserve injectives (23.5.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: δ-functor axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: A (cohomological) δ-functor from abelian category A to B is a collection of additive functors T^i : A -> B (T^i = 0 for i < 0) together with morphisms δ^i : T^i(A'') -> T^{i+1}(A') for each short exact sequence 0 -> A' -> A -> A'' -> 0, satisfying (i) the long exact-sequence property (the induced sequence is exact) and (ii) functoriality with respect to morphisms of short exact sequences (commutativity of δ's).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived functors are examples of δ-functors; this axiomatization abstracts their key properties (Section 23.2.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal δ-functor and uniqueness property
rubrics_metrics.description: A δ-functor (T^i,δ^i) is universal if for any other δ-functor (T'^i,δ'^i) and any natural transformation α : T^0 -> T'^0 there is a unique morphism of δ-functors extending α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: there is at most one universal δ-functor extending a given left-exact functor T^0; key theorem (23.2.8) and Corollary (23.2.10) give sufficient conditions for universality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient condition for universality (Theorem 23.2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (T^i,δ^i) is a covariant δ-functor and for every object A there exists a monomorphism A ↪ J with T^i(J) = 0 for all i > 0, then (T^i,δ^i) is universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark: hypotheses may be weakened to require only that each T^i is effaceable; references to Weibel/Lang for proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: right derived functors give a universal δ-functor
rubrics_metrics.description: If A has enough injectives and F is a left-exact covariant functor A -> B, then the right derived functors R^iF (with the accompanying δ^i) form a universal δ-functor (Corollary 23.2.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: embed objects into injectives and use vanishing of higher derived functors on injective objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry of Tor (Exercise 23.3.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an isomorphism Tor^A_i(M,N) ≅ Tor^A_i(N,M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: take free resolutions of both M and N, form a double complex (their 'product'), and use spectral sequence arguments with both orientations to deduce symmetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derived functors via acyclic resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: If F : A -> B is right-exact and A has enough projectives, an object A∈A is F-acyclic if L_iF(A)=0 for i>0. Derived functors of F on an object B can be computed by taking a resolution of B by F-acyclic objects (not just projectives), truncating, applying F, and taking homology (Exercise 23.3.C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields practical flexibility: e.g., Tor can be computed using flat resolutions (flat = F-acyclic for tensor). The construction uses building a projective resolution of a complex (Hint 23.3.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartan–Eilenberg resolution (resolution of a complex)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a complex C• in an abelian category, one can construct a Cartan–Eilenberg injective resolution I_{*,*} (a double complex of injectives) whose rows/columns are injective resolutions of the cycles, boundaries, and cohomology of C•, satisfying compatibilities (Exercises 23.3.E–G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to set up the double complex needed for the Grothendieck spectral sequence and to compute derived functors of compositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grothendieck composition-of-functors spectral sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: If F : A -> B and G : B -> C are left-exact additive covariant functors, A and B have enough injectives, and F sends injectives of A to G-acyclic objects of B, then for each X in A there is a spectral sequence with E^{p,q}_2 = R^qG(R^pF(X)) converging to R^{p+q}(G∘F)(X) (Theorem 23.3.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses injective resolutions, applying F and then taking a Cartan–Eilenberg resolution and applying G, and analyzing the resulting double complex with two spectral sequence orientations (Sections 23.3.6–23.3.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leray spectral sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism of ringed spaces π : (X,O_X) -> (Y,O_Y) and any O_X-module F, there is a spectral sequence with E_2 term H^q(Y, R^pπ_* F) abutting to H^{p+q}(X, F) (Theorem 23.4.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an immediate application of the Grothendieck spectral sequence once one checks that π_* sends injective O_X-modules to acyclic objects for H^0 (pushforward of injectives are acyclic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category of O_X-modules has enough injectives (Theorem 23.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ringed space (X,O_X), the category Mod_OX has enough injectives: for any O_X-module F one can embed it into an injective O_X-module constructed from skyscraper sheaves at points and products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction outline: at each stalk choose inclusion into injective stalk module, form skyscraper injectives Q_p and take product Q' = ∏_p Q_p; prove F -> Q' is injective by checking stalks (Exercises 23.4.A–C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flasque (flabby) sheaf definition and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheaf F on a topological space is flasque if all restriction maps res_{V,U} : F(V) -> F(U) are surjective for every inclusion U ⊂ V. Properties: (a) in a short exact sequence 0->F'->F->F''->0 if F' is flasque then sections over any open set give exact sequence (23.4.D); (b) pushforward of a flasque sheaf is flasque (23.4.E); (c) injective sheaves are flasque (23.4.H); (d) flasque sheaves are Γ-acyclic (Hi(X,F)=0 for i>0, Exercise 23.4.I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flasque sheaves serve as acyclic objects for computing derived functor cohomology; extension-by-zero i! and adjointness are useful tools in proofs (23.4.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension by zero functor properties (i!)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an open embedding i: U ↪ Y, the extension by zero i! : Mod_OU -> Mod_OY is defined by (i!F)(W)=F(W) if W ⊂ U and 0 otherwise (on the presheaf then sheafify). Properties: (a) (i!F)_q = F_q for q∈U and 0 otherwise; (b) i! is exact; (c) (i!, i^{-1}) is an adjoint pair, so Hom_OY(i!F, G) ≅ Hom_OU(F, G|_U) (Exercises 23.4.F–G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use i! to relate local injectivity/acyclicity to global statements and to prove injectives are flasque.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible absence of enough projectives for Mod_OX
rubrics_metrics.description: The category Mod_OX of O_X-modules on a ringed space need not have enough projectives (e.g., X = P^1_k with Zariski topology and O_X the constant sheaf Z); there may be no surjection from a projective sheaf onto certain sheaves like Z_q (section describing counterexample).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: do not assume availability of projective resolutions in sheaf categories; work with injectives or acyclic/flasque resolutions instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement of Čech and derived functor cohomology under hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a quasicompact separated scheme and F is a quasi-coherent sheaf, then Čech cohomology of F (for finite affine covers) agrees with derived functor cohomology H^i(X,F) (Theorem 23.5.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: choose finite affine open cover and injective resolution, form double complex of sections on intersections, and use spectral sequences; key vanishing ingredients are (A) injective sheaves have vanishing higher Čech cohomology for finite covers, and (B) on affines RiΓ(F)=0 for i>0 (Section 23.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right adjoints to exact functors preserve injectives
rubrics_metrics.description: If (F,G) is an adjoint pair of additive functors between abelian categories with F exact, then the right adjoint G sends injective objects to injective objects (Exercise 23.5.B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used e.g. in proving that restriction of an injective sheaf to an open subset is injective (Exercise 23.5.A).
